patients.summary: High school math teacher who joined in 2021 with autoimmune hypothyroidism, developed type 1 diabetes in May 2022 managed by endocrinology, and had three pregnancies with outside obstetrics: two vaginal deliveries (the second with a macrosomic infant and neonatal hypoglycemia) and a third ending in cord prolapse and emergency cesarean after her last practice visit.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to join the practice. Teaches math at the high school, can only come in after 3 pm or during summer break. Currently on thyroid medication through her old doctor, about 3 refills left. Explained membership and that insurance still covers labs and specialists. New patient slot given for 6/8 at 3:30. Release of information form emailed; she returned it signed the same afternoon and it was sent to her prior office.

conditions.note: Autoimmune; thyroid peroxidase antibodies positive at prior practice

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning on an empty stomach

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Pages from her previous primary care office, scanned.

Problems: hypothyroidism, autoimmune, first found in March 2018; thyroid peroxidase antibodies positive. Started levothyroxine and settled at 75 mcg daily; TSH in range on that dose at the last two checks.
Medications: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily.
Allergies: none known.
Surgeries: none.
Family history: father type 1 diabetes, mother hypothyroidism (autoimmune), sister celiac disease.
Health maintenance: Pap smear 2020, negative for intraepithelial lesion. HPV vaccine series completed as a teenager. COVID-19 vaccine (Pfizer) 4/9/2021 and 4/30/2021 per state registry printout.

Reviewed and abstracted by PCP.

social.value: Social, a glass of wine some weekends

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25F joining the practice, teaches high school math. Came straight from school.

HPI: Feels well. Hypothyroid since 2018 (antibody positive per old records), on levothyroxine 75 mcg each morning, takes it before coffee, rarely misses. No palpitations, weight stable, energy fine now that the school year is ending.

PMH: hypothyroidism. PSH: none. Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily. Allergies: none known.
FH: dad has type 1 diabetes, mom hypothyroid, sister has celiac.
SH: married, no kids yet. Never smoked. Wine on some weekends, a glass or two. No drugs. Runs a couple of times a week.
Gyn: regular cycles. Pap 2020 normal at prior office. HPV series done as a teen.
Imm: COVID x2 this spring.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Well appearing. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules felt. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Skin normal. No edema.
PHQ-9: 2.

A/P
1. Hypothyroidism, autoimmune: continue 75 mcg. TSH today.
2. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids; one-time HIV and hep C screens discussed and drawn. Pap due 2023. Flu shot in the fall.
3. Given the family history of type 1 diabetes and celiac, reviewed symptoms worth calling about (thirst, urinating a lot, weight loss).

RTC 9 months for a physical, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Maya, good to meet you on Tuesday. Everything came back normal: thyroid level right where we want it on the 75 mcg, blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and both screening tests (HIV and hepatitis C) negative. No changes. I'll send your levothyroxine to the pharmacy with a year of refills.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after school for flu shot. No fever today, no prior reactions. VIS given. Quadrivalent flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Waited 15 minutes, fine, left for parent-teacher night.

documents.title: Pharmacy immunization notice
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Notification from community pharmacy: Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 booster dose administered 11/17/2021, right deltoid. Entered into the immunization record by MA.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. 25F. No complaints. Busy with a calculus section added this year, sleeping 7 hours. Running less over the winter.
Thyroid: no missed doses, no symptoms.
Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg. NKDA.
SH unchanged: never smoker, occasional wine. FH: father T1DM, mother autoimmune hypothyroid, sister celiac.
ROS negative including thirst, urination, weight change.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Well. HEENT normal, thyroid smooth and normal size. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd benign. Ext without swelling. Skin no rashes.
PHQ-9 1.

A/P: healthy adult with treated hypothyroidism.
- TSH, CMP, lipids.
- Pap next year.
- Flu and COVID up to date for this season.
Follow up in a year.

documents.title: Acute Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning asking to be seen.

S: About 3 weeks of being thirsty all the time, getting up twice a night to pee, and keeping a water bottle on her desk she refills between classes. Pants looser; down about 4 kg from March on our scale. Appetite normal to increased. Some blurry vision at the end of the day. No nausea, vomiting, belly pain or shortness of breath. No fevers. Thyroid pill taken daily.
Father was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes as an adult, so she recognized the pattern.

O: Vitals as charted, weight 59.4 kg. Looks well, not ill or dry. Breathing comfortable, no fruity odor. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.
Urine dip in office: glucose positive, ketones negative, protein negative.

A/P: new hyperglycemia in a lean 25-year-old with weight loss and a strong autoimmune family history. Type 1 (autoimmune) diabetes is most likely.
- BMP and A1c sent stat.
- Called endocrinology directly; they will see her Friday 5/13.
- Reviewed when to go to the ED: vomiting, abdominal pain, fast breathing, confusion.
- Plenty of water, avoid sugary drinks.

Addendum 18:55: glucose 287, bicarbonate normal, A1c 10.4%. Called her with results. She is feeling the same, no vomiting. Plan unchanged, keep Friday appointment.

documents.title: Nurse check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt on her lunch break per PCP. Still thirsty, no vomiting, eating and drinking fine. Confirmed endocrinology Friday 5/13 at 9:00, she has a sub arranged for her morning classes. Faxed yesterday's labs and visit note to endocrinology. ED precautions repeated, she verbalized them back.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, consultation of 05/13/2022, received by fax.

Reason for referral: new hyperglycemia (glucose 287 mg/dL, HbA1c 10.4%), referred by her primary care physician.

Ms. Pereira is a 25-year-old teacher with three weeks of polyuria, polydipsia and weight loss. Her father has type 1 diabetes; she has autoimmune hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 75 mcg. No ketosis on her office urine.

Exam: lean build. No acanthosis. Thyroid normal. No signs of dehydration.

Labs drawn here: GAD65 antibody 48 U/mL (reference <5), positive. C-peptide 0.4 ng/mL with a simultaneous glucose of 241 mg/dL. Tissue transglutaminase IgA negative (screened given her sister's celiac disease).

Impression: type 1 diabetes mellitus, new onset, autoimmune.

Plan:
1. Insulin glargine 16 units subcutaneously at bedtime.
2. Insulin lispro with meals, 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate. Carbohydrate counting session with our diabetes educator completed today.
3. Fingerstick glucose before meals and at bedtime; log reviewed by phone weekly for now.
4. Hypoglycemia recognition and treatment taught.
5. Return in 3 months; A1c through your office is fine.
6. Annual dilated eye exam recommended.

Allergies: NKDA.
Medications on our list: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, insulin glargine, insulin lispro.

Thank you for this referral.
Endocrinology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u 2 weeks after new type 1 diabetes. Endocrinology letter reviewed (GAD65 positive, C-peptide low; on glargine 16 at bedtime and lispro 1 unit/10 g with meals).

S: Thirst gone within a few days of starting insulin. Fasting sugars still above goal, daytime readings closer. One mild low before lunch after a fire drill made her late to eat; treated with juice, felt fine. Learning to count carbs, using an app. Emotionally "a lot to absorb", but her dad has been a good coach. Keeping glucose tabs in her desk.

O: Weight 60.6 kg, up from 59.4. BP and HR as charted. Feet: skin intact, monofilament normal, pulses 2+.

A/P
1. Type 1 diabetes, new: per endocrinology. Weekly log calls with their educator. Will draw A1c in August before her endo follow-up.
2. Vaccines indicated with diabetes: PCV20 and hepatitis B (first of three) given today.
3. Referral for a dilated eye exam this summer.
4. Hypothyroidism: levothyroxine 75 mcg, stable.
5. Letter for school nurse to allow snacks/glucose checks in class: done.

documents.title: Hepatitis B dose 2
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Second hepatitis B vaccine, IM right deltoid. Tolerated the first dose without problems. Third dose due in November, reminder set.

documents.title: Ophthalmology eye examination
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology, exam of 07/14/2022.
Indication: type 1 diabetes, diagnosed 05/2022; baseline exam.
Visual acuity 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS. Pressures normal. Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy either eye; macula flat, no edema. Optic nerves healthy.
Impression: no diabetic retinopathy.
Plan: repeat dilated exam in 12 months.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: A1c result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Maya, your A1c is down a long way from May. Real progress in three months. I've forwarded it to endocrinology for your visit next week.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology follow-up, 08/22/2022.
Type 1 diabetes, diagnosed 05/2022. Recent A1c from her primary care office reviewed and much improved.
Meter download: pre-meal readings in range most of the day, but fasting values persistently above target. Two mild lows in July, both explained by exercise.
Plan: increase glargine to 22 units at bedtime. Continue lispro 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate. Discussed continuing to log. Follow-up 6 months.
Allergies: NKDA. Other meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily.

documents.title: Prior authorization request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: insurer requires prior authorization for the insulin lispro pens at the new quantity after the dose change. Endocrinology is the prescriber; called their office, they will submit. Pt informed by portal that she has enough pens for about 10 days. 9/8: endo office confirms approval through 9/2023.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (quadrivalent) left arm and bivalent Pfizer COVID booster right arm. Feeling well, no fever. Observed 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: Hepatitis B dose 3, lab draw
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Third and final hepatitis B dose IM left deltoid; series complete. A1c drawn per PCP standing order. Pt says fasting numbers are better since the glargine increase. No lows needing help from anyone.

documents.title: A1c result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c improved again, close to 7 now. Nice work. Copy to endocrinology. Your hepatitis B series is done.
